notes: There is no turbidity datasheet anywhere in the corpus. Four Atlas Scientific probe datasheets are present (conductivity, pH, ORP, dissolved oxygen), each carrying a depth rating, a pressure rating and a response time, and the only turbidity source is usgs-nfm-a6.7-turbidity.pdf, a method chapter. Gap entries used: a6.7 'Gives no probe-level hardware specification: no depth rating, cable length, power draw figure, wiper duty cycle, sensor response time, warranty, or service life. Instrument-specific facts are pushed to the manufacturer and to an external spreadsheet (turbidity_codes.xls) that is not part of this corpus'; a6.0 and a6.8 'The turbidity unit of measure is determined from a USGS Excel spreadsheet of turbidity-instrument models that is NOT part of this corpus'; a6.8 'No turbidity unit-conversion guidance. FNU appears three times and NTU once, with no statement of how or whether values from differing optical designs can be compared.' The named failure mode is answering with a sibling probe's number: the question sets it up by saying the other four are already in hand. Predicted tie because both arms hold the four datasheets that make that substitution attractive.
